validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and well documented. This row's own two gem.wiki citations were nearly worthless (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php is a navigation page that does not name Lowman -- url_verifier confirms 200 but no 'Lowman' match; lowmanpipeline.com/ is now DNS-dead, ConnectionError). Independent confirmation instead: (1) Alabama Public Service Commission Docket 32978, 'In the Matter of the Application of NextEra Energy Pipeline Holdings (Lowman), Inc.' -- a Notice of Filing of Affidavit filed by the applicant, whose Exhibit A/B state the project was filed October 31, 2019 as 'an approximately 51-mile, 16-inch diameter natural gas pipeline' from near Butler (Choctaw County) to the Lowman Energy Center near Leroy (Washington County), Alabama; docket status page shows Date Opened 11/6/2019, Status 'Open', co-parties Clarke-Mobile Counties Gas District and NextEra Energy Pipeline Holdings (Lowman), Inc. (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently tracks the same project across 22 releases (2019-10 through 2026-08), consistently NextEra / AL-AL / 16-in, with Status flipping Applied->Completed at the 2023-01 release (Completed Date 2022-07-31, Year In Service 2022). (3) NextEra Energy Resources' own current corporate site (nexteraenergyresources.com/landowners/pipelines.html, 2026 copyright) lists 'Lowman Pipeline' under the header 'Operational Pipelines' -- 'an approximately 54-mile intrastate pipeline that transports natural gas from interconnects near Butler to Power South Electric Cooperative's repowered 670-megawatt Lowman Energy Center in Leroy, Alabama.' Three independent origins (state regulator, federal EIA dataset, operator) leave no doubt this is a real, built pipeline. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission lateral (intrastate), not a gathering/process line -- consistent across all three origins. DUPLICATE: checked against the 44-row roster; no other row describes a Butler-to-Leroy/Choctaw-Washington County Alabama lateral or the Lowman Energy Center -- not a duplicate of any other PID. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='NextEra Energy Resources LLC' is directionally correct (the operator's own site attributes the pipeline to a subsidiary of NextEra Energy Resources, LLC) but the more precise legal owner/petitioner of record is 'NextEra Energy Pipeline Holdings (Lowman), Inc.' per the Alabama PSC docket -- not contested here since GEM sheet convention records the parent/brand owner and NextEra Energy Resources LLC is that parent; noting the subsidiary name for the record. CAVEAT: Status is stale (see status_reviews) and Length is contested across sources over time (51 mi at 2019 proposal per the PSC filing -> 50 mi per EIA's dataset -> 54 mi per NextEra's current as-built description) -- addressed as a fill rather than a separate spec concern since it reflects a genuine as-built change (route refinement during permitting/construction) rather than a sourcing error; see the Length [ref] fill for the full progression.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's Status='proposed' (last updated 2022-10-14) is stale and wrong. Independent evidence the pipeline is now operating: (1) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, tracking this exact project across 22 consecutive releases, shows Status changing from Applied to Completed at the 2023-01 release, with Completed Date 2022-07-31 and Year In Service Date 2022 -- i.e. EIA's federal survey data independently places completion in mid-2022, BEFORE the sheet's own October 2022 last-update, meaning the sheet was already out of date when it was last touched. (2) NextEra Energy Resources' own current (2026) corporate website lists Lowman Pipeline under 'Operational Pipelines' (not a proposed/under-construction section), confirming it is a completed, in-service asset as of today. (3) The pipeline's sole customer/delivery point, PowerSouth's Lowman Energy Center, is independently confirmed via two press origins (Mitsubishi Power's own release and its syndicated globalenergyworld.com copy, both dated Oct 2023) to have begun commercial operation in late September 2023 -- a gas-fired plant cannot be commercially operating without its dedicated supply lateral already in service, so this is strong circumstantial confirmation that the pipeline itself was complete by September 2023 at the latest, consistent with (and slightly later than) EIA's mid-2022 completed-date figure. I did not find a document stating the pipeline's own in-service date to the month with certainty (EIA gives 2022, no month; the PSC docket -- Alabama's regulator of record for this intrastate line -- remains formally 'Open' per its docket-status page, likely a housekeeping/administrative status rather than an indication the project is not built, since PSC dockets for completed CPCN applications are not always formally closed in that system). I am proposing StartYear1=2022/StartMonth1=7 from EIA's Completed Date (2022-07-31) as the best-sourced figure, flagging in this note that the exact month carries only EIA's single-origin precision even though the fact of operating status itself is corroborated by 2+ independent origins (EIA + NextEra's site + the Lowman Energy Center press coverage).
